title: PhasePilot by Transition Bio

beats.heading: PhasePilot
beats.subtitle: A closed loop for mapping phase separation — live on Beta3.
beats.presenter: This is PhasePilot, our closed loop that lets Muse run phase-separation experiments.

beats.heading: Condensates organise the cell

lines.text: The right molecules, in the right place, at the right time.
Condensates help organise the cell, droplet by droplet.
When they misfire: cancer and neurodegeneration.

beats.presenter: Condensates organise the cell, and when they misfire they drive cancer and neurodegeneration.

beats.heading: Every protein has a phase map

lines.text: Proteins demix into dense droplets, like oil in water.
Each protein has its own phase diagram, highly multidimensional.
With compound, the boundary rises: less phase separation.

beats.presenter: Phase separation is demixing into dense droplets, and mapping each protein's diagram shows how compounds shift it.

beats.heading: PhaseScan: droplets as experiments

lines.text: Each droplet = 100 pL = one experimental condition.
Droplets are imaged in three fluorescence channels.
A CNN calls each one mixed or phase separated, live.
~1,000,000x less protein per data point than conventional labware.

beats.presenter: PhaseScan turns each 100-picolitre droplet into one condition, using about a million times less protein.

beats.heading: Dimensions multiply the work

lines.text: k levels per n variables = k^n conditions.
100,000 at 5 variables; 1,000,000 at 6, for 10 levels.
Time is proportional to t0 times k^n, for just one protein.
Past four or five parameters, a comprehensive scan is impossible.

beats.presenter: Every new dimension multiplies the work as k to the n, so past four or five variables a full scan is impossible.

beats.heading: We handed it to Muse

lines.text: Muse proposes conditions. PhaseScan runs the droplets.
SAM checks the images. The Bayesian model updates.
Muse can only choose: run / replicate / pause / finish.
Every setpoint is checked by the instrument controller.

beats.presenter: So we handed the experiment to Muse in a closed loop, with the controller checking every setpoint it proposes.

beats.heading: Live today on Beta3
bullets: G3BP1 / PolyA RNA / PEG — live run, 4 November 2026
Muse chose each setpoint from the live evidence
Each decision arrived with Muse's explanation of why
beats.note: Real phone footage: the PhasePilot dashboard on the rig monitor during today's live run.
beats.presenter: This is live today: G3BP1, PolyA RNA and PEG on Beta3, with Muse choosing each setpoint and explaining why.

beats.heading: The Beta3 rig in the lab
bullets: Syringe pumps and chip stage, close up, today
PhaseScan runs each condition in microfluidic droplets
Images stream straight into SAM and the Bayesian planner
beats.note: Real phone footage from the lab today, shown inside a Transition Bio frame.
beats.presenter: And this is the real Beta3 rig in our Cambridge lab, running the droplets Muse asked for.
Our real dashboard has four panels: decisions, Muse reasoning, SAM QC, and results with the phase map.
SAM segments every real droplet and outlines its condensates; green is accepted, red rejected, and only passes count.
Here you can read Muse's written reasoning for a decision, exactly as it arrived during the run.
The Bayesian planner updates after every round and steers sampling toward the boundary, so the map sharpens where the information is.

beats.heading: Replay: same map, far less work

stats.sub: 2.5 uL instead of 52 uL in the 3-variable replay
2.9 min instead of 51 min in the 3-variable replay
Versus the full scan — G3BP1 / TDP-43 / RNA

beats.footnote: A 17x saving buys log_k(17) extra dimensions at every n; a raster costs k^n, the loop samples the boundary, ~k^(n-1).
beats.presenter: In replay against the full scan, PhasePilot matched the boundary while using twenty times less protein and seventeen times less instrument time.

beats.heading: From weeks to days
beats.sub: Legacy scan vs PhasePilot, with guides at 1 week and 1 month.
beats.green_line: +1 variable at 10 levels in the same instrument time and protein; +2 at 4 levels.
beats.presenter: At six variables that saving turns thirty-six instrument days into two, and buys at least one extra variable in the same budget.

beats.heading: One loop, any parameter space

lines.text: Biology is high-dimensional.
Protein, RNA, binding partners, phosphorylation, pH, temperature.
Phase separation is demonstrated here; the template travels.
One closed loop for automated experiments well beyond phase separation.

beats.presenter: Biology is high-dimensional, so one closed loop that maps any parameter space becomes a template far beyond phase separation.

beats.heading: PhasePilot
lines: Muse chooses. PhaseScan runs. SAM checks.
The Bayesian model keeps the phase map.
